name: Mount Tsurugi from Murodo (剱岳)
why: The hardest of the popular Japanese Alps summits: from the Murodo plateau over Bessan pass to a hut under the granite towers, then chains and ladders to the 2,999 m top.
book: No permit. Reach Murodo on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route: train from Toyama to Tateyama, cable car to Bijodaira, bus to Murodo (about 2 hours in all). Book Kenzan-so or Tsurugisawa-goya ahead for the night.
water: Water and drinks at Murodo and at the huts (Tsurugigozen-goya, Kenzan-so). Carry 1.5 litres for the summit day: there is none above Kenzan-so.
dangers: Between Ippuku-tsurugi and the summit, falls from ledges and falling rock are a constant risk: wear a helmet; a harness, sling and carabiners to clip the chains are recommended.
Kani-no-tatebai (up) and Kani-no-yokobai (down) are one-way chain and ladder sections on sheer rock: queues on weekends.
Snow lingers in the gullies into July and returns in October; outside the season it is a winter mountaineering climb.
Afternoon thunderstorms on bare rock: leave Kenzan-so for the summit at dawn.
turnaround: Not at Heizo col (the foot of Kani-no-tatebai) by 08:30, or rain on the rock: go back to Kenzan-so. Wet chains on granite are not a place to be.

points.name: Murodo
points.note: 2,450 m, the Alpine Route bus terminal. Walk past Mikurigaike pond and down the steps to the Raichodaira campsite.

points.name: Tsurugigozen-goya at Bessan pass
points.note: About 2,750 m, 2 h 50 min from Murodo after the long rocky climb from Raichodaira. Mount Tsurugi appears across the Tsurugisawa valley.

points.name: Kenzan-so hut
points.note: Night 1 at about 2,475 m, under the north face, after a traverse down from the pass. Start for the summit before 05:00.

points.name: Tsurugidake summit, over the chains
points.note: 2,999 m, reached in about 2.5 hours from Kenzan-so over Mae-tsurugi and the Kani-no-tatebai chains. Descend by Kani-no-yokobai and the same way to Murodo.
